metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:embedding_collapse_score: (mean off-diagonal cosine + 1)/2 on up to 2048 nonpadding item embeddings, isolated seed 42. Directional alignment only; 0.5 means mean cosine zero. Does not measure recommendation diversity or embedding rank.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:pos_neg_margin_mean: Mean positive-minus-sampled-negative logit over nonpadding pairs from at most ten loader batches and 256 sequences, further limited to reserve the frozen paired panel. In-sample, dependent on loader sampling, and scoped to the primary view rather than a four-category macro.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:pos_neg_margin_p10: Nearest-rank lower tenth percentile of sampled margins.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:pos_neg_neg_beats_pos_rate: Fraction of sampled margins strictly below zero.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:pos_neg_small_margin_rate: Fraction of sampled margins below 0.5; raw score scale affects this measurement.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:pos_neg_margin_count: Number of valid sampled positive-negative positions; missing estimates are null.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:pos_neg_margin_category_br: Unsupported: item categories are unavailable. Empty category lists are not evidence of no category effects.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:rank_change: Perturbed target rank minus original rank; positive is worse. Diagnostic ranks use score descending, item ID ascending ties.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:hit10_change: Perturbed indicator(target rank <= 10) minus original indicator, within the same 100 diagnostic candidates.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:top10_overlap: Size of original/perturbed top-ten set intersection divided by ten.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:feature_cosine: Cosine between final-position features; null when either feature has zero norm.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:aggregation: Replicates averaged within each user, users averaged within each category, then all four required categories equally. Missing categories produce null macro entries; truncation suppresses the macro entirely.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:ci95: 1000 paired user-bootstrap resamples within each category using isolated SHA256-derived seeds; percentile interval. All panels are small (at most 32 users/category). Excludes training-seed variability and adaptive-selection bias; singleton intervals are degenerate.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:perturbations: k=min(3,max(1,floor(prefix_length/5)),prefix_length-1). Oldest/recent deletions compact survivors; recent deletion changes the last conditioning item. Five random-deletion and five last-item-preserving prefix-shuffle replicates use frozen indices. Random last-item changes are separately flagged per replicate.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:position_control: Unsupported without verified per-layer key/value masking and preserved position IDs. Even a supported control would retain attention-renormalization and distribution-shift effects.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:data_scope: Final public training interaction is the target and preceding retained history is the prefix. These targets may already have been trained on. No held-out labels, ratings, review text, item categories, prices, stores, or simulator traits are used.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:validation: Diagnostic candidates and tie rules are independent of the pinned host evaluator. No host users, exclusions, ranking semantics, or splits are changed. Sensitivity and bootstrap intervals do not establish validation improvements.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:experiment_status: Only a frozen descriptive hypothesis list is recorded. No intervention training, validation query, or predictive-value claim is performed here. A training-side launcher must establish pre-validation timing, matched baseline/configuration/checkpoints, and explicit remaining shared GPU budget before running it.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:accounting: Elapsed synchronized wall time includes manifest generation, sampled probes, scoring, and summaries; it is a conservative local diagnostic cap checked before encodes, not GPU event time or a replacement for host shared-budget accounting. An in-flight encode or CPU summary may finish beyond the cap.
